title: Conduct investigations with legal and evidentiary discipline: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: What makes an artifact defensible evidence for this investigation?
focalInsight: Definitions, decision owner/criterion, failure consequence, and retrieval remain distinct.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Investigation Authority
nodes.definition: Authority: legal, contract, privacy, employment, and purpose limits scope

nodes.label: Evidence Preservation

altSummary: Definitions, decision owner/criterion, failure consequence, and retrieval remain distinct.
textFallback:
investigation authority: Authority: legal, contract, privacy, employment, and purpose limits scope. Decision: decide authorized lead before collection.. Failure/example: admin searches unrelated employee device.
evidence preservation: Preservation: protect original and context before remediation. Decision: decide hold/acquisition order.. Failure/example: wipe destroys provenance.
chain of custody: Custody: document collector/time/location/transfer/access. Decision: decide whether handler change is attributable.. Failure/example: artifact cannot be linked to collector.
legal hold: Hold: suspend normal deletion for scoped material. Decision: decide with counsel/authority.. Failure/example: retention job deletes relevant log.
forensic integrity: Integrity: hash/validated method supports unchanged artifact. Decision: decide acquisition verification.. Failure/example: analysis alters sole original.
investigation roles: Roles: separate authority, custodian, examiner, reporter. Decision: decide need-to-know.. Failure/example: examiner self-approves scope.
reporting documentation: Report: state method/facts/limits/recipients. Decision: decide disclosure path.. Failure/example: raw artifact presented as conclusion.
investigative techniques: Technique: authorized reasoning/method, not tool. Decision: decide fit to question.. Failure/example: unsupported inference.
forensic tools: Tool: validated acquisition/analysis aid. Decision: decide known limits/version.. Failure/example: unvalidated parser changes timestamps.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: What makes an artifact defensible evidence for this investigation?
learningContract.misconception: A system owner or interesting artifact authorizes unlimited collection.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
learningContract.focalInsight: Definitions, decision owner/criterion, failure consequence, and retrieval remain distinct.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: No universal tool/configuration or legal conclusion.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: Use the stated decisive scenario to select owner, control/evidence, and escalation.
